bothSidesReview.eligibility: Trigger met: "a formal opposition letter or statement from a named organization" (docs/BOTH-SIDES.md). The Alliance for Pharmacy Compounding published a dated opposition post (2026-07-10, per the page own structured data) that is not a passing mention but an organised campaign -- an emergency member town-hall briefing, a member survey portal collecting shortage-compounding data, and planned instructions for messaging the Senate HELP Committee. Support is equally on the record: a bipartisan sponsor pair with a joint announcement, a named American Diabetes Association officer quoted in it, and a dated Alliance for Safe Biologic Medicines statement (2026-02-16) endorsing H.R. 6509 by number. NOT false balance: no opposition was sought out to fill a slot; the opposition found the article, not the reverse. The section says explicitly that H.R. 6509 has no recorded vote rather than implying a contested one, and every position that could not be sourced to a stored file was removed or left out (see the omission rows).
bothSidesReview.verbSymmetry: PASS. Verified mechanically against scripts/tracker-gate.js own ASYMMETRIC_VERBS regex over the extracted section: 0 hits across two independent runs. Verbs in use -- supporters: says, supports, argues, says. Opponents: wrote, says, puts...at, argues, illustrates. Both sides get the same neutral says/argues pairing the rulebook prescribes; neither side gets a validating verb set against a doubting one for the other. Confirmed by a second-round Sonnet reviewer independently of the script.
bothSidesReview.stripTest: PASS, reviewed sentence by sentence twice. Every argumentative clause is grammatically subordinate to a named holder -- the sponsors joint announcement, Rita Kalyani of the ADA, ASBM, APC. The only sentences in the site own voice are structural record facts (no recorded vote; the committee ordered S. 3794 reported), never contested characterisations. Two framing words were deliberately kept OUT of the site voice during this audit: "FDA-approved" as a synonym for "commercially available" (ASBM vocabulary, not the statute) and any restatement of APC allegation about who wrote the bill.
bothSidesReview.vehicleBill: HUMAN-VERIFIED 2026-08-31 (Opus, in-conversation, in the main thread), across every vehicle the stored Congress.gov record discloses, asserting nothing from memory. (1) H.R. 6509 own record: three actions, all dated 2025-12-09, referral to Energy and Commerce and nothing since; one text version; one committee activity, the referral; no floor action; not law. (2) relatedbills for H.R. 6509 returns EXACTLY ONE bill -- S. 3794, SAFE Drugs Act of 2026, CRS-identified as a Related bill. (3) The link is reciprocal: S. 3794 own relatedbills returns exactly one bill, H.R. 6509. There is no third vehicle anywhere in the record. (4) THE FINDING THIS CHECK EXISTS FOR: the policy has moved, just not under the tracked number. Senate HELP ordered S. 3794 reported favorably with an amendment in the nature of a substitute on 2026-07-22; Sen. Cassidy reported it without a written report on 2026-07-27; it went onto the Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders as Calendar No. 524 the same day. All three actions post-date the article 2026-07-17 publication, and the frozen article mentioned the Senate nowhere at all. (5) Unlike KOSA, the substitute text IS published -- S. 3794 carries two text versions, Introduced in Senate and Reported to Senate. The article says so and is explicit that it describes H.R. 6509 as introduced, the only version the House bill has; it does NOT describe the substitute contents, which were not read for this audit. (6) Neither bill has become law. LIMIT OF THE CHECK, stated honestly: relatedbills in both directions is what the stored record can show. It would not reveal SAFE Drugs language riding an appropriations bill or a user-fee reauthorisation under a number Congress.gov does not link, and no stored source was available to test that.

claims.claim: ADDED: the "What the Bill Would Change" list was built entirely from the official CRS summary, and the summary omits Section 5 of the bill. Section 5 strikes the $15,000 base establishment fee in 21 U.S.C. 379j-62(c)(1)(A)(i) and replaces it with a Secretary-determined amount. A specific dollar figure being removed from statute is substantive, and the bill text is a registered source, so the article now carries it in a paragraph that says explicitly that the summary does not mention it.
claims.sourceSpan:
a base amount deemed appropriate by the Secretary to fund
activities to ensure the safety of compounded drug products
claims.note: COVERAGE finding, not a faithfulness finding - the qa-loop step 2.7 class (faithful is not the same as complete). Found by the hostile Sonnet verifier, which read the bill text against the summary; no scripted gate looks for it.

claims.claim: CORRECTED: the draft said APC "asked its member pharmacists to send messages to the Senate committee that handled the companion." The stored page shows that as a FUTURE item - "Then watch your email for two important messages next week: Instructions for sending a message directly to members of the Senate HELP Committee via an upcoming call to action portal." The asks APC actually makes in the post are the town-hall sign-up and the member survey. Rewritten to match, and the post is now dated from its own metadata.
claims.sourceSpan: Then watch your email for two important messages next week
claims.note: Tense/aspect error: a planned action reported as an accomplished one. Caught by the hostile Sonnet verifier reading the surrounding context, not by any span check - the words were all present, in the wrong tense.

claims.claim: CORRECTED before the verifier round, and independently confirmed by it: the draft said "the sponsors say" of two phrases that are press-office copy - one the third-person lede, one an unattributed Key Provisions bullet. Neither appears in Yakym or Carson own quoted remarks, which are different sentences entirely. Reworded to "Their joint announcement says." Neither member is quoted directly anywhere on the page.
claims.sourceSpan: Americans deserve confidence that their prescription medicines are safe, effective, and made to highest quality standards
claims.section: Why do supporters back the bill?
claims.note: Same class as the KOSA Blackburn/Blumenthal quote-boundary finding and the NDAA FY2027 Johnson/Jeffries misquotes. Caught here by a fresh context read of the source around each span. It also protects a live trust-page claim: articles/how-we-source-quotes.html promises every quotation attributed to a member of Congress is verbatim from the Congressional Record, so a press-release member quote on this page would have falsified it.

claims.claim: REWRITTEN: the lede described the limits as applying to compounded drugs that are "essentially a copy" of "commercially available, FDA-approved products." The bill and the CRS summary both say "commercially available drug product"; the bill defines that term by commercial sale and section 501(a)(2)(B) manufacturing compliance, not by FDA approval. "FDA-approved" is ASBM framing, not the statute. Changed to the bill own term.
claims.sourceSpan:
essentially a
copy of a commercially available drug product
claims.note: Small but real: it imported an advocacy group vocabulary into the site neutral voice.

claims.claim: CORRECTED in the main thread, by a fresh context read rather than by any span check: the ADA quotation was first cut to begin at "concerns have emerged," dropping the concessive opening of the same sentence - "While compounded medications play a critical role in our health care system." Truncating there made a diabetes association sound categorically hostile to compounding when its own sentence starts by defending it. The second quotation was cut at "compounding practices," which broadened a call for oversight that she scopes to specific medication classes. Both were extended to the full source clauses.
claims.sourceSpan: While compounded medications play a critical role in our health care system, concerns have emerged regarding the widespread availability
claims.section: Why do supporters back the bill?
claims.note: The quote-boundary class in its less obvious direction: not words put in a mouth, but a qualifier taken out of one. A verbatim-span gate cannot see it - both truncations were verbatim. Only reading the sentence around the span exposes it.

claims.claim: CORRECTED in the main thread: the first draft of the Section 5 paragraph described the $15,000 figure as the base establishment fee 21 U.S.C. 379j-62(c)(1)(A)(i) sets "for outsourcing facilities." Section 5 of the bill says no such thing - it names the section and the figure and nothing else, and no stored source establishes whose fee it is. The qualifier came from prior knowledge, which is not a source. Removed.
claims.sourceSpan: SEC. 5. BASE ESTABLISHMENT FEE.
claims.note: Out-of-source qualifier class, the one CLAUDE.md names as structurally invisible to the figure guards. Self-caught on the fresh read before either verifier round saw it.
